Name: TSQL_STRING_CORE
Feature: CONCAT(arg1, arg2, ...), CONCAT_WS(separator, arg1, arg2, ...), STRING_AGG(expr, separator) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...), LEN(expr), DATALENGTH(expr), CHARINDEX(substr, str [, start]), PATINDEX(pattern, expr), SUBSTRING(expr, start, len), STUFF(expr, start, len, replace_expr), REPLACE(expr, from_expr, to_expr)
Description: Core T-SQL string processing and concatenation functions.
CONCAT/CONCAT_WS are safer than '+' because they handle NULL more predictably.
LEN excludes trailing spaces, while DATALENGTH returns byte count (important for NVARCHAR).
CHARINDEX and PATINDEX provide 1-based position search; PATINDEX supports wildcard patterns.
STRING_AGG is the primary row-to-string aggregate in SQL Server.
Examples: SELECT STRING_AGG(name, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY name) FROM dbo.t;
EffectiveSQLs: SELECT CONCAT('prefix-', CAST(id AS varchar(20))) FROM dbo.t;
